text.p: Cambodia on Saturday welcomed the Association of Southeast Nation's (ASEAN) decision to admit it, together with Burma and Laos, to the grouping in July.
"Oh good, that's good for Cambodia," Information Minister Ieng Mouly told Reuters.
"Now we'll be part of the region, we can play a role in the region. We can contribute and particapate," he said.

The seven-member ASEAN met on Saturday and decided to admit the three at the grouping's annual ministerial meeting in Kuala Lumpur on July 24-25. There had been some concern that the entry of the three into ASEAN -- comprising Burma, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam -- would take place at a December summit, not in July, partly because of political instability in Cambodia.
A feud between the two leaders of Cambodia's coalition government has led to deadlock in parliament, preventing the passing of key legislation necessary for ASEAN mebership.
"I think this means they didn't take into consideration the internal problems," Ieng Mouly said of the decision.
